A long-sleeved V-neck cotton T-shirt, a real plain T-shirt and not a real garment, covered edge to edge in a bold flat-colour illustration with thick black outlines, designed to make the shirt look like the outfit of a Balinese temple dancer. The print covers every part of the shirt from the ribbed collar band to the hem and out to both sleeve hems, and wraps around the side seams to the back. The outfit is printed across the whole front, over the shoulders and down both sleeves, showing a gold-braided costume with a sash. The print wraps all the way round, the back of the shirt shows the rear of the outfit from the back collar to the hem and along both sleeves. The outfit's fabric runs seamlessly over the shoulders and down the sleeves, every part of the shirt in the outfit's own colours and textures. It is an ordinary T-shirt in shape, with a straight open hem and sleeves cut to match the outfit's sleeves. Only the upper garment is printed, running all the way down to the shirt's straight hem. The outfit's collar meets the real collar band, its shoulders sit on the real shoulder seams and its sleeves fill the real sleeves, all in one piece of printed cloth. The outfit is laid out on the shirt's own rectangle shape, fully covering it from side seam to side seam. The shirt is a long-sleeved T-shirt matching the outfit's long sleeves, printed with the sleeves and cuffs all the way down to the wrist hems. The shirt is solid opaque cotton and every texture and sheen is a printed picture. Only the outfit's fabric, trims and fastenings are pictured, spread across the entire shirt as a continuous pattern. It is a flat print, not a framed picture, not a small centred graphic, not a standing figure and not a drawing of a garment on a hanger. It carries enough of the costume to be unmistakable, the belt, straps and buckles of the outfit, the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem and its pockets, flaps and trims, all in the outfit's own colours.

The outfit's front panels run straight down the shirt's front with its shoulders sitting on the shirt's shoulder seams, and its sleeves are printed along the shirt's sleeves to cuffs at the sleeve hems, showing a long embroidered vestment. The back of the shirt is printed just as completely, edge to edge, with the back of the same outfit, its back collar, shoulder blades and the backs of both sleeves. The outfit's fabric runs seamlessly over the shoulders and down the sleeves, every part of the shirt in the outfit's own colours and textures. The shirt keeps the outline of an ordinary T-shirt, round neckline, straight side seams, sleeves, and a straight open hem. Only the upper garment is printed, running all the way down to the shirt's straight hem. The outfit's cloth runs unbroken from the collar band across both shoulders and down both sleeves to their hems, so every part of the shirt is outfit cloth. The outfit is stretched to the shirt's own straight-sided shape and fills it completely, so it suits any body size. The shirt is cut sleeveless, with armholes where the outfit's sleeves would start. All textures, transparencies and sheens are printed patterns on solid cotton. The print is the garment itself, flat and unfolded over the shirt, in its own cloth and colours. It may also show a flat printed bare chest in __clothing_uniform_tee_skin__ with printed chest hair where the outfit is worn open, all as flat ink. It also shows a printed collar continuing the outfit up to the neckline and printed cuffs where the sleeves end. Tiny printed shadows and fold lines suggest the garment without any real depth. The tee is clearly a costume tee, not a plain shirt, it shows the outfit's patches, insignia and emblems, its pockets, flaps and trims and the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem, so anyone can tell at a glance what outfit it stands for.
